original_question: If (X_n) is an increasing sequence of sets of reals each satisfying Omega choose Gamma (that is, S1(Omega,Gamma)), must the union also satisfy Omega choose Gamma?
target_in_paper: Section 5, Problem 5.2 ([35]): Does every union of an increasing sequence {X_n}_{n∈ℕ} of sets satisfying \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma} satisfy \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}?
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target: it has the right property, S1(Ω,Γ) (the Gerlits–Nagy γ-property), the right operation, namely countable increasing unions, and the right ambient class, sets of reals.
missing_details: The paper formulates the question universally: for every countable increasing sequence X1⊆X2⊆⋯ of sets of reals, with X=⋃n Xn.
The nearest official formulation uses the notation \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}; immediately before Problem 5.2 the paper notes that S1(Ω,Γ)=\binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}.
Ω and Γ are families of open covers: an open ω-cover U of X is a nontrivial open cover with X∉U such that every finite F⊆X is contained in some U∈U.
A γ-cover is an infinite open cover such that each x∈X belongs to all but finitely many members of the cover.
Open covers are taken in the subspace topology inherited from ℝ, since the chapter is working with sets of real numbers.
The chapter explicitly restricts attention to sets of real numbers in this problem.

The nearby context explains why this question matters: Miller observed that a negative answer would also give a negative answer to Problem 5.1 on the δ-property, because increasing unions preserve the δ-property.
refined_question: Let X=⋃_{n∈ℕ} X_n, where X_1⊆X_2⊆⋯ are sets of real numbers with the subspace topology from ℝ. Assume that each X_n satisfies \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma} (equivalently, S1(Ω,Γ)); that is, every open ω-cover of X_n contains a γ-subcover, where an open ω-cover is a nontrivial open cover such that every finite subset of X_n is contained in some member, and a γ-cover is an infinite open cover each point of X_n belongs to all but finitely many members. Must X also satisfy \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, if X_1⊆X_2⊆⋯ are sets of real numbers and each X_n satisfies S1(Ω,Γ), must ⋃_{n∈ℕ} X_n also satisfy S1(Ω,Γ)?
justification: This is the exact nearby problem your draft is aiming at. In Section 5, after defining the δ-property and stating that S1(Ω,Γ)=\binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}, the paper asks precisely whether every union of an increasing sequence of sets satisfying \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma} again satisfies \binom{\Omega}{\Gamma}. The introduction provides the notation S1(A,B), the meanings of ω-cover and γ-cover, and the standing scope restriction to sets of real numbers. The sentence immediately before Problem 5.2 gives the contextual reason for the question by linking a negative answer to Problem 5.1.
